title: [SDK 52] expo-location background permission promise resolves denied before the iOS response
body: On iOS with Expo SDK 52 and the new architecture disabled, I have to call `await Location.requestBackgroundPermissionsAsync()` twice. After I grant foreground access with “Allow While Using App” and choose “Change to Always Allow” in the background prompt, the first call reports that permission was denied as if I canceled it. Pressing the button again then reports the permission that I already granted. I reproduced this in a development build, Expo Go, and a standalone app. My Snack reproducer is https://snack.expo.dev/@brodanoel/background-location-broken. I am using Expo 52.0.23, React Native 0.76.5, and the managed workflow on iOS.

symptoms_visible: After I choose “Change to Always Allow” in the iOS permission dialog, the first `requestBackgroundPermissionsAsync()` call reports denied as if I canceled it.
Calling the same method a second time reports the background permission that I already granted.
N0.label: N0 premature denied result reported

symptoms_visible: When foreground access has already been granted and I later request background access, the background request returns denied before I have answered the permission prompt.
N1.label: N1 legitimate permission-upgrade flow established

symptoms_visible: I implemented the suggestion, but when foreground permission has been granted for the map and background permission is requested later, the background request still returns denied before my response.
N1_x.label: N1_x background-only guidance aftermath

symptoms_visible: In the minimal repository and recording, the background permission dialog is still awaiting input when the JavaScript request has already produced a denied result.
N2.label: N2 timing bug reproduced and regression narrowed

symptoms_visible: With my AppState workaround, I wait for the app to become active and then read the background permission again; the production flow now observes the permission I selected.
N3.label: N3 AppState workaround installed

symptoms_visible: On a build containing the native fix, the background permission request waits for my response and returns the final permission status without a second call or AppState workaround.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: Why do you need to request foreground and background permissions separately?
Are both permissions requested together, or can background access be requested much later?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My app has a map that only needs foreground location and a separate background-check feature that most users never use. A user can grant foreground access for the map and only request background access months later, so asking everyone for Always access up front is not appropriate.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I do not have separate features; I always need background tracking immediately and can request only background authorization on first launch.
The background feature is enabled days rather than months after the map feature.

question_patterns: Can you confirm whether it reproduces when foreground permission is granted and background permission is requested in the same app session?
What exact ordering reproduces the premature denied result?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. I request foreground access, grant it, and then request background access in the same session. The background call returns denied without waiting for my answer, even though the iOS dialog is displayed.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It only happens after terminating and relaunching the app; requesting both permissions in one session always waits correctly.

question_patterns: Did this same flow work on an earlier Expo SDK?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The same flow worked without this issue on SDK 51 with the old architecture. After upgrading to SDK 52, the background request started returning denied before I answered.

question_patterns: Is requesting Always authorization after When In Use a valid iOS flow?
Do you have an example of another iOS app upgrading location permission later?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. Apple documents requesting Always authorization after When In Use, and I attached an example of the Citizen app presenting the permission upgrade as a separate feature flow.

edges.comment: Comments c9, c12-c15, and c19-c21 are folded into one simulated user side. They establish that this is a supported, delayed permission-upgrade use case and a regression from SDK 51, rather than two unnecessary simultaneous requests.

solution.intent: Avoid the foreground-to-background upgrade flow on iOS and request only background permission, relying on that request to obtain foreground access automatically.
solution.concrete_example: On iOS, skip `requestForegroundPermissionsAsync()` and call only `await Location.requestBackgroundPermissionsAsync()` when location access is needed.

edges.comment: Comments c4-c10, c14, c28, and c32-c38: background-only guidance did not address the reporter's real delayed-upgrade flow, and the reporter stated that implementing the suggestion did not remove the premature denied result.

question_patterns: Can you provide a minimal public repository containing only the permission flow and reproduction instructions?
Please share a standalone reproduction outside Snack.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I created a minimal repository with reproduction instructions: https://github.com/participant3/expo-location-repro. It requests foreground permission and then background permission in the same session.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The minimal repository does not reproduce the issue; the background request waits correctly unless I add my application's other native modules.
The same minimal sequence reproduces from a different public repository.

question_patterns: Can you record the reproduction and show when the returned status appears relative to the iOS dialog?
Does the JavaScript promise finish before you respond to the background permission prompt?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. In my recording, the background permission dialog is still on screen and I have not selected anything, but the app has already received denied. I attached the reproduction notes and demo.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The promise remains pending while the dialog is open and returns denied only after I tap Don't Allow.

question_patterns: Can you narrow this to a change in expo-location or identify which native requester began behaving differently?
Did you find a likely regression in the SDK 52 native implementation?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: After investigating, I found that the behavior was introduced by PR #29272 and involves `EXBaseLocationRequester.m`. Reverting and patching that file is a possible temporary option.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Reverting PR #29272 makes no difference, and the same premature result occurs with the SDK 51 native requester.

edges.comment: Comments c16-c18, c26, c39-c42: multiple affected users are folded into one simulated user side. The raw reproduction visibly establishes the timing. The final interpretation of why the native requester completes early remains engineer-side.

solution.intent: Use an AppState-based temporary workaround: after requesting background permission, wait for iOS to return the app to the active state and then query the permission again.
solution.concrete_example: Request foreground permission first. Call `requestBackgroundPermissionsAsync()`, and if the app became inactive for the iOS prompt, listen for `AppState` to return to `active`; then call `getBackgroundPermissionsAsync()` and use that result. Remove the listener afterward.

edges.comment: Comments c25 and c27-c30: the reporter adapted this workaround and confirmed it was working in production. It restores the application flow but does not repair expo-location's incorrectly timed promise.

solution.intent: Fix the SDK 52 iOS native location requester so `requestBackgroundPermissionsAsync()` remains pending through the authorization UI and resolves from the completed authorization result, then have the reporter verify the same-session foreground-to-background flow on a build containing the fix.
solution.concrete_example: Patch the SDK 52 regression in `EXBaseLocationRequester.m` associated with PR #29272 so the background request is not completed with the current denied value merely because the app becomes inactive while iOS presents the Always authorization prompt. Resolve it after the authorization callback/state update, and ask the reporter to retest the foreground-then-background sequence in a build containing the patch.
solution.inference_hint: The users supplied the timing evidence, SDK comparison, public reproducer, and pointer to PR #29272/EXBaseLocationRequester.m. Concluding that the SDK 52 requester resolves from an intermediate denied state when the permission UI makes the app inactive—and therefore must wait for the native authorization completion—is the engineer's synthesis.

edges.comment: Comment c42 acknowledges reproduction specifically when foreground permission is followed by background permission in the same session and commits to a native fix. Verification of a build containing that fix is terminal-side and is not required diagnostic evidence.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause as an Expo SDK 52 iOS native requester regression: `requestBackgroundPermissionsAsync()` completes with an intermediate denied state while the system authorization prompt is still unanswered, instead of waiting for the final authorization result.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the same-session public reproduction, the recording showing denied before user input, the SDK 51 comparison, and the investigation pointing to PR #29272 and `EXBaseLocationRequester.m`.

Must not dismiss the use case by recommending that iOS applications always request only background permission; requesting Always authorization after an earlier When In Use grant is a legitimate flow, and that guidance was tried without resolving the reported behavior.
An AppState-active listener followed by `getBackgroundPermissionsAsync()` may be offered as a temporary workaround, but it must not be presented as the native fix.
The actual fix must make the native background permission request wait for authorization completion and return the final status.
Must ask the reporter to verify the foreground-then-background flow on a build containing the native fix before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced React Native and Expo application developer who can maintain a Snack, discuss production permission flows, adapt asynchronous AppState workarounds, and compare SDK behavior; other technically capable affected developers contribute a public native reproducer and regression investigation and are folded into the same simulated user side.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct, persistent, and evidence-driven. Explains product constraints with concrete scenarios, quotes code and documentation, challenges advice that does not fit the use case, and becomes emphatic when the observed behavior is treated as a misunderstanding.
